look_here_first: Pine muhly (Muhlenbergia dubia): densely tufted narrow-leaved perennial with erect slender stems and a narrow contracted panicle. Confirm with membranous ligule (about 4–10 mm) and measured spikelets (about 3.8–5 mm); never identify from habit alone.

field_id_lesson.look_here_first: A dense perennial tuft with fine often involute leaves and narrow erect gray-green panicles; not a broad pink cloud of flowers.
crew_checkpoints: Check basal tussock versus creeping/rhizomatous growth
Photograph an entire attached mature narrow panicle
Measure the membranous, acute-to-lacerate ligule (4–10 mm according to Flora of North America); don't infer it from habit photos.
Measure mature spikelets (3.8–5 mm) and glumes (mostly 2–3 mm), then compare awn and lemma; requires magnified photo with scale.
Compare with Muhlenbergia rigens and M. lindheimeri using multiple characters, not just fountain habit
photo_handoff: Single mature spikelet and glumes with millimeter scale
Mature panicle macro and branch spacing

fna_measured_diagnostic_review_20261023.lookalike_difference: FNA distinguishes M. rigens by pine muhly's looser panicle, longer ligules, olive-green anthers and often longer lemmas.

field_id_finish_pass.stage: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS — new true source-attributed leaf-junction, flowering head and reproductive close-ups installed and pictured; photographed membranous part not mm-calibrated or source-vouchered, glumes/lemma not dissected
field_id_finish_pass.crew_teaching_summary: PINE MUHLY = densely tufted, non-rhizomatous perennial with narrow rolled blades and erect gray-green, contracted but not rigidly spikelike panicle. Important test against deergrass: open attached collar and measure long 4–10(12) mm membrane ligule; inspect mature small spikelet with paired shorter glumes and longer lemma. The two current photos document only gross habit: NOT ligule, glumes or lemma. Do not equate pine muhly with nonexistent Muhlenbergia piniflora.

measured_diagnostic_key.growth_form: Densely cespitose perennial, not rhizomatous; culms roughly 30–100 cm; narrow usually inrolled blades about 1–2 mm wide.
measured_diagnostic_key.ligule: Firm membranous ligule, often acute/lacerate, FNA 4–10 mm; Kew GrassBase 4–12 mm. TRUE free membrane must be photographed at attached sheath/blade junction with 1 mm ruler.
measured_diagnostic_key.panicle: Contracted gray-green panicle; Flora of North America 10–40 cm long and 0.6–2.4 cm wide, with stiff primary branches up to 7 cm, often ascending rather than strict spikelike cylinder. Kew describes narrower commonly 10–30 cm form.
measured_diagnostic_key.spikelets: Solitary one-fertile-floret spikelets approx. 3.8–5 mm (FNA); Kew approximately 4–5 mm. Source literature, not measurements made from photographs.
measured_diagnostic_key.glumes: Pair approximately equal, shorter than lemma, ~2–3 mm, faintly one-veined.
measured_diagnostic_key.lemma_awn: Lemma approximately 3.8–5 mm, narrowly lanceolate, three-veined, hairy callus, awn variable including awnless or straight awned; FNA awns to ~6 mm, GrassBase gives 0–4 mm. Never identify a presumed awn from the habit photo.
measured_diagnostic_key.anthers: Anthers ~1.5–2.2 mm, olivaceous or greenish; color depends on reproductive stage and photography.

compare_deergrass.first_clue: Deergrass usually has a more rigid, narrower, denser spikelike panicle. Pine muhly has looser ascending branches and can reach 2.4 cm across.
compare_deergrass.ligule: Pine muhly ~4–10(12) mm versus deergrass FNA 0.5–2(3) mm; capture several mature leaves of BOTH species at the same scale.
compare_deergrass.lemma: Pine muhly ~3.8–5 mm versus deergrass ~2.4–4 mm; ranges overlap. Distinguish after specimen dissection.
compare_deergrass.flower_anthers: Pine typically greenish/olivaceous; deergrass yellow or purple, but color is supporting evidence only.
compare_deergrass.caution: Not reliably separated by tuft silhouette or one old flowering head photo; record actual ligule and lemma measurements.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · DISSECT THE LEMMA, CALLUS AND AWN
field_id_short_tiles.cue: Fertile lemma about 3.8–5 mm; a single terminal awn may be absent or short.
field_id_short_tiles.expand: The FNA treatment gives fertile lemmas about 3.8–5 mm, with an awn absent or to 6 mm; Kew GrassBase describes a 4–5 mm, three-veined lemma and a 0–4 mm awn. Preserve these source-specific ranges. Dissect a mature same-voucher spikelet: separate its two shorter one-veined glumes, expose the three-veined lemma, two-veined palea, hairy callus and any true awn attachment. An entire grass head, finger for scale, or undissected narrow floret is NOT proof of bract identity, awn origin or dimensions.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES + RELEASE GATE
field_id_short_tiles.cue: Separate deergrass by its shorter ligule and usually tighter panicle; don't rely on silhouette.
field_id_short_tiles.expand: Deergrass (M. rigens) has a generally shorter membranous ligule, often 0.5–2(3) mm in FNA, and typically a more rigid, spikelike panicle; pine muhly has a longer 4–10(12) mm ligule and usually less rigid flowering branches. Their lemma lengths overlap. Lindheimer muhly (M. lindheimeri) forms a much larger fountain-shaped bunch, and seep muhly (M. reverchonii) has a more open fine-textured panicle. Do not confuse accepted M. dubia with the held source name M. piniflora or certify county nativity from it. NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: rooted local crown connected to mature head, 1-mm-calibrated true ligule, same-voucher 3.8–5 mm spikelet with both glumes, lemma, palea, callus and any awn, matched deergrass. NEEDS_SITE_QA: verify seven archived photos and comparison panels, research-grade/voucher vs provisional labels, all licenses/attribution, actual arrows and public mobile display. Retain FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS.
